title: sprintcard-latency-cost-comparison-draft-aug2029
content:
Purpose:
This note collects an experimental sweep we ran to compare two session-handling approaches (coalesced sessions → single thermal slot vs independent routing → per-request scheduling) across three mixed workloads. Aim: provide a compact, shareable artifact ("sprintcard") for product and infra stakeholders summarizing p50/p90/p99 latency and $/1M-token cost tradeoffs under realistic session mixes.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Coalesced sessions (session-affinity + small time-window coalescing) reduces $/1M tokens by ~12–28% for conversational-heavy workloads while increasing p99 by 5–18ms in the highest-concurrency cases.
- Independent routing (no affinity, best-effort multiplexing) gives slightly better p99 at high sustained qps but suffers on cost for workloads with many short multi-turn sessions.
- Recommendation: default to coalesced mode for PLG and mid-market customers with <200 qps per tenant, offer independent routing for extreme low-latency enterprise tiers.

Experiment design:
- Hardware: 8xA100-equivalent GPU pool (single availability zone), runtime build: rtd-2029-07-31.
- Models: open-chat-13b quantized FP16 profile (2-token warmup kvcache enabled).
- Workload profiles (all runs 60k requests sample, 95% CI ~±2%):
  * Chat-Long: 30% long sessions (avg 12 turns, 800 tokens per session), 70% short queries.
  * Conversational-Burst: many small sessions (avg 3 turns), intermittent bursts to 600 qps.
  * Embeddings-Mix: 50% short chat, 50% embedding requests (single-turn).
- Policies compared: COALESCE-W2 (coalesce window 200ms, affinity by session-id), INDEP (stateless routing, per-request slot assignment).
- Cost model: token-based compute minutes mapped to $/1M tokens using internal price sheet (includes amortized GPU time + scheduling overhead).

Observed metrics (aggregated):
Table: per-workload median latency (ms) and cost ($/1M tokens)
Workload | Policy   | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1M tokens
---------|----------|---------|---------|---------|-------------
Chat-Long| COALESCE | 64      | 112     | 210     | 42.8
Chat-Long| INDEP    | 59      | 108     | 196     | 55.6
Conv-Bst | COALESCE | 39      | 84      | 162     | 47.2
Conv-Bst | INDEP    | 36      | 78      | 145     | 61.9
Emb-Mix  | COALESCE | 51      | 98      | 188     | 38.0
Emb-Mix  | INDEP    | 50      | 94      | 179     | 44.3

Interpretation notes:
- Cost differences are driven primarily by reduced kernel invocation overhead and better KV cache reuse in COALESCE mode for multi-turn sessions. That amortizes GPU startup and increases batching efficiency.
- p99 penalty in COALESCE appears when short bursts collide with long-session coalesced slots -> observed queuing for the tail. This is most visible in Chat-Long at sustained concurrency > 320.

ASCII visualizations (compact sprintcard style):
1) Relative cost bars (lower is better) – normalized to INDEP for each workload
Chat-Long: COALESCE [█████████ ] 0.77 | INDEP [████████████] 1.00
Conv-Bst : COALESCE [██████████] 0.76 | INDEP [████████████] 1.00
Emb-Mix  : COALESCE [████████ ] 0.86 | INDEP [██████████] 1.00

2) p99 delta (COALESCE minus INDEP, positive = worse)
Chat-Long: +14ms  [+++++++ ]
Conv-Bst : +17ms  [++++++++]
Emb-Mix  : +9ms   [++++  ]

Session-size impact (mini sweep):
- For sessions with avg-turns >=8, COALESCE wins cost by ~30% with negligible p50 impact.
- For avg-turns <=2 (micro interactions), INDEP slightly wins latency and cost parity narrows.

Edge cases observed (notes for SRE):
- When a single tenant generates an oscillating pattern (rapid start/stop sessions), COALESCE's coalescing window occasionally groups unrelated sessions leading to transient KV contamination metrics. We flagged this in telemetry (see linked PR).
- Under multi-tenant isolation settings with small per-tenant quotas, COALESCE causes visible slot hogging if eviction thresholds not tuned.

Risk matrix (short):
- Customer impact: Medium (tail sensitivity)
- Operational overhead: Low (policy is an infra flag)
- Rollback complexity: Low (can switch routing at layer 3)

Actionable recommendations (next sprint):
1) Ship a conservative default: enable COALESCE-W2 for trial & standard tiers, with automatic fallback to INDEP when observed p99 delta > 25ms for >10k requests/day per tenant.
2) Add telemetry: per-tenant coalescing hit-rate, kvcache reuse ratio, and per-slot tail-queue length.
3) Implement fast-eviction heuristics to avoid long-session hogging when per-tenant quotas active.
4) Run a follow-up A/B for enterprise customers (INDEP as control) focusing on p99 SLA compliance for 4 weeks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What threshold for auto-fallback balances product experience vs cost? (propose start = 20ms p99 delta over 24h)
- Confirm cost model assumptions for mixed embeddings with 4x different kernel profiles (embedding kernels cheaper per-token but higher overhead).
- Validate results on a different instance family (L40x) to ensure kernel selection doesn't invert cost advantage.

Appendix: quick run commands and flags used
- run harness: bench/run_sprintcard.sh --profile chat-long --policy COALESCE-W2 --samples 60000
- telemetry query snippet: select tenant, coalesce_hit, kv_reuse, tail_queue from telemetry.coalesce_rollup where day >= '2029-08-01'

Notes to reviewers:
This is a compact working artifact intended for rapid consumption by product and infra. The charts are intentionally textual (sprintcard) so they can be embedded in Slack threads and review decks without recreating images. Please comment with additional metrics you'd like surfaced (e.g., energy per token, amortized disk IO).
